newsitem.title: USA: Ill. COPs lawsuit verbal settlement - paper.
newsitem.headline: Ill. COPs lawsuit verbal settlement - paper.

text.p: Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar and Democratic lawmakers have reached a verbal agreement to settle a lawsuit challenging the issuance of $19.2 million of certificates of participation for a state public aid building, Chicago Tribune reported Wednesday.

State Rep. Jeffrey Schoenberg, D-Evanston, and other House Democrats filed the lawsuit in June 1996 contending that the Illinois Department of Central Management Services exceeded its constitutional and statutory authority by issuing the certificates as part of a lease-purchase agreement.

The settlement requires good faith efforts by Republicans to work on passing comprehensive reform legislation and Schoenberg told the Tribune he was confident remaining differences can be resolved before the fall veto session of the Illinois General Assembly.

Motions to dismiss the lawsuit will be filed in Cook County Circuit Court soon, the Tribune reported. With formal dismissal of the lawsuit, the state can begin using the downtown building for the new Department of Human Services, the newspaper said.
